policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word order only (αὐτῷ ἐγγίζοντες / ἐγγίζοντες αὐτῷ); ASV 'were drawing near unto him' renders either identically and no note is mapped here (the 3:12 note concerns publicans).
ASV 'both the Pharisees and the scribes' renders the correlative τε ... καί; the omission would give only 'and'.

ASV 'having lost one of them' is a participle coordinate with 'having a hundred sheep'; the subjunctive ἀπολέσῃ would give a conditional 'if he lose', as ASV in fact renders the parallel subjunctive at 15:8 ('if she lose one piece').
Word order only; ASV 'one of them' is the same English for ἐξ αὐτῶν ἓν and ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν.
ASV 'his shoulders' renders the simple possessive; it does not mark the reflexive ἑαυτοῦ ('his own') against αὐτοῦ.
Word order only; 'there shall be joy in heaven' is compatible with either arrangement of ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ and ἔσται.
οὗ and ὅτου are equivalent in ἕως οὗ / ἕως ὅτου; ASV 'until' cannot distinguish them, and the only note here glosses drachma.
Active συγκαλεῖ and middle συγκαλεῖται both yield ASV 'she calleth together her friends'; the English marks no middle voice.
The variant adds only the article τὰς before 'neighbors'; ASV's 'her friends and neighbors' shows no article and would not in either case.
Word order only; 'there is joy' renders γίνεται χαρά and χαρὰ γίνεται alike.
ASV opens 'and the younger of them said', and ASV renders both δέ and καί as 'and'; the mapped note ('Greek the.') concerns the article rendered 'thy substance', not this connective.
πάντα and ἅπαντα are the same word intensified; ASV 'gathered all together' renders either.
Purely a matter of the adjective's form agreeing with λιμός; ASV 'a mighty famine' is the same English for ἰσχυρά and ἰσχυρός.

ASV text reads 'have filled his belly' = γεμίσαι τὴν κοιλίαν αὐτοῦ, and the mapped textual_variant note puts the rival χορτασθῆναι ('have been filled') in the margin as 'Many ancient authorities read'.
ἔφη and εἶπεν both give ASV 'he said'.
Middle περισσεύονται and active περισσεύουσιν both yield 'have bread enough and to spare'; the English marks no voice difference.
ASV 'I perish here with hunger' renders ὧδε, which excludes the RP reading that omits it; between λιμῷ ὧδε and ὧδε λιμῷ the English word order decides nothing.
ASV begins the verse 'I am no more worthy' with no connective; the added καί would have been rendered 'and I am no more worthy', as ASV renders καί throughout this chapter.
Both ἑαυτοῦ and αὐτοῦ give ASV 'his father'; the English does not distinguish reflexive from simple pronoun here.
Word order only; 'And the son said unto him' renders either sequence of ὁ υἱός and αὐτῷ. The mapped note concerns the addition at the end of the verse, not this unit.
ASV has 'in thy sight: I am no more worthy' with no connective before οὐκέτι; the RP καί would appear as 'and I am no more worthy'.

ASV text ends the verse at 'to be called thy son' and relegates 'make me as one of thy hired servants' to a mapped textual_variant note ('Some ancient authorities add'), so the shorter reading is the one rendered.
ASV 'Bring forth quickly the best robe' renders Ταχύ, which the RP reading omits.
The variant adds only the article τήν; ASV 'the best robe' supplies the definite article either way and cannot mark it.
ASV 'and bring the fatted calf, and kill it' has 'bring' as an imperative coordinate with 'kill'; the RP participle ἐνέγκαντες would give 'having brought the fatted calf, kill it'.
ASV punctuates asyndeton — 'is alive again; he was lost' — with no connective before the clause; the RP reading's καί would have produced 'and he was lost'.
The modal particle ἄν leaves the optative εἴη unchanged in English; ASV 'what these things might be' renders the clause with or without it.
ASV 'But he was angry' renders the adversative δέ; οὖν is inferential and ASV renders it 'therefore' or 'so', never 'but'.
ASV 'said to his father' has an unitalicized 'his' answering αὐτοῦ; where ASV renders a bare article as a possessive in this chapter it notes it (15:12, 'Greek the.'), and no such note stands here.
The variant adds only the article τῶν before 'harlots'; ASV 'with harlots' shows no article either way.
Word order and article placement only; 'the fatted calf' renders σιτευτὸν μόσχον and μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν alike.

ASV 'is alive again' matches the wording it uses at 15:24 for the same clause, so the 'again' follows the parable's repeated formula and does not by itself mark the ἀνα- prefix of ἀνέζησεν against ἔζησεν.
ASV 'and was lost' carries 'was' over from the preceding 'was dead' whether or not ἦν is expressed; the added copula is invisible in the English.
